description: Fabric 26.2 client mod that finds structures and biomes from the world seed

releases.notes:
You can now tell Structure Map about the world border. Run `/structurelocate border auto` to use the one the server has, or set your own with `border <radius>` or `border <x> <z> <radius>`. There's also a button for it in Settings. Once it's set, searches skip anything outside it, and setting it clears out the located structures and Structure Map waypoints that were outside. Waypoints you made yourself are left alone. It's saved per server and per dimension, and `border off` removes it.

Ancient city waypoints are always dark aqua now, so they're easy to pick out on the map. Waypoints added from a god apple search are called "Ancient City - God Apple" or "Desert Pyramid - God Apple" instead of just the structure name.

I also fixed a bug where unchecking a structure with the delete setting on could add back a waypoint that was never there.

For Minecraft 26.2 with Fabric Loader 0.20+ and Fabric API.

Hotfix for the god apple search. On some worlds `/structurelocate godapples` stopped with a "Cannot invoke ... getGameTime()" error. The cause was ancient cities with candles sitting in water: working out their chests tripped over a water update. That's fixed, and if a structure ever can't be worked out now, the search just skips it and keeps going instead of giving up.

Also, it says "ancient cities" now, not "ancient citys".

mods.name: Structure Map
mods.description: Finds structures and biomes from the world seed, using vanilla world generation on the client.

releases.notes:
For Minecraft 26.2 with Fabric Loader 0.20+ and Fabric API.

You can now check structures off once you've been to them. Tick the box next to one in `/structurelocate menu`, or hit the [✓ Done] button that now shows up on search results in chat. After that, searches act like it isn't there: `/structurelocate structure` gives you the next closest one, and the waypoint and god apple searches just reach a bit further to make up the numbers.

Checked-off rows go grey in the menu, and there's a switch to hide them. Untick one if you want it back.

It also deals with the Xaero waypoint. By default the waypoint gets disabled, so it's still in your list but off the map. If you'd rather it got deleted, or left alone, that's in the new settings screen: the Settings button in the menu, `/structurelocate settings`, or Structure Map's config button in Mod Menu. Unticking undoes it either way, so a deleted waypoint comes back too.

mods.name: Structure Map
mods.description: Finds structures and biomes from the world seed, using vanilla world generation on the client.

releases.notes:
For Minecraft 26.2 with Fabric Loader 0.20+ and Fabric API.

Every structure you find with `/structurelocate` now goes into a list you can actually browse, instead of scrolling back through chat for coordinates. Open it with `/structurelocate menu`, or bind "Open located structures" in Controls.

Pyramids and ancient cities show how many god apples are in their chests. If you found one with a plain search, it checks the chests in the background and the count pops up a moment later. Click the God apples heading and the best ones go to the top, with everything that has none dropping to the bottom.

You can also filter by structure type, sort by distance, or flip on God apples only. Click a row to copy its coordinates. Every row has a Waypoint button for Xaero's Minimap, and pyramids and ancient cities have a Chests button that shows exactly what's in each chest.

The list is saved per world seed, so it survives a relaunch. It only shows the dimension you're in.

`/structurelocate godapples ancient_city` now goes up to 50 instead of 10.

For Minecraft 26.2 with Fabric Loader 0.20+ and Fabric API.

New: `/structurelocate godapples pyramid` and `/structurelocate godapples ancient_city`. They tell you which nearby structures have an enchanted golden apple in a chest, and give you that chest's coordinates. Add a number (up to 10) to get more than one.

It works the loot out from the seed instead of visiting. The server decides each chest's loot when the chunk generates, so the mod rebuilds the structure, places its pieces in the same order the server does to get each chest's loot seed, and rolls the loot table from there.

I checked it against a real world: 65 chests across 3 pyramids and 2 ancient cities, and every loot seed and item matched what the server put there. The nearest result usually comes back in a second or two.

Two catches. Some ancient city chests come after a sculk patch in the same chunk, and sculk spread depends on caves, so those can't be predicted and get skipped (roughly 1 in 50). And if someone already opened the chest on your server, it won't have what was predicted.

It needs the seed, like everything else in Structure Map: from Seed Cracker, single player, or `/structurelocate seed`.
